text:
Yes. Monzo can temporarily restrict or “freeze” an account—for example, if it spots unusual activity, suspects someone else may have access, or needs to meet legal or financial-crime obligations. A restriction doesn’t necessarily mean you’ve done anything wrong, and it may affect only some features.

**If it happens:**
1. Check the Monzo app for what’s restricted and whether Monzo needs information from you. Reply to requests through the app.
2. If you can’t use the app, call Monzo in the UK on **0800 088 4040** or email **help@monzo.com**. Monzo says urgent queries are handled 24/7; less urgent phone or chat support is available 7am–8pm.
3. If the restriction means you can’t afford essentials such as food or medication, tell Monzo that explicitly.
4. If you’re unhappy with how it’s handled, you can make a complaint in the app or email **complaints@monzo.com**. If you’re still dissatisfied after Monzo’s final response, you may be able to take it to the Financial Ombudsman Service, usually within six months.

Monzo says it may not be able to explain the precise reason for a restriction in some cases, and reviews can take different amounts of time.
